Window types / W-01

Casement windows

Hinged on the side and cranked open outward. When it closes, the sash presses against the frame all the way round, which gives the tightest seal of any opening window.

Estimate online Request a quote
Operation
Side-hinged, opens outward
Frame depth
82.6 mm · 3 1/4"
Frame edge to glass
77.8 mm · 3 1/16"
Glass
Dual or triple pane
Profile section

How it is built

A casement is two welded PVC parts: the frame fixed in the wall and the sash that carries the glass. From outside you see mostly sash, about 3 1/16" from the edge of the frame to the glass.

The glass is set from the room side and held by a glazing bead, so nothing that holds it can be reached from outside. The screen sits on the inside.

Where it fits

  • Bedrooms and living rooms
  • Above counters and sinks, where a crank is easier to reach than a sash
  • Beside a picture or fixed unit, to bring air into a large opening

Glass

  • Double or triple pane sealed units
  • Low-E coatings, argon fill
  • Warm-edge spacer bars
  • Tempered glass where code requires it
  • Obscure / frosted glass for bathrooms
  • Internal grilles in several patterns

Frame & hardware

  • White, or laminated exterior colours and woodgrains
  • Multi-point locking hardware
  • Integrated screens
  • Brickmould, jamb extensions and nailing fin to suit your wall
  • Custom sizes and shapes
